availability.note: Mazda AU CX-60 page served model code C60CAW5P50EP4 with live Victorian prices on the research date (build & price renders no data to automated fetches; the page's embedded configurator data was read instead). Seven P50e price lines: Pure, Evolve, Touring, GT, Azami, Azami SP, Azami Takumi.

listPrice.note: CarExpert 23 Aug 2026 price table headed 'Price before on-road costs'; same figure in CarExpert's 2026 P50e GT review (Aug 2026) and GoAuto 23 Jul 2026 ('Pricing excludes on-road costs'). Cross-check against Mazda's own Victorian figure on https://www.mazda.com.au/cars/cx-60/: $61,970 (RDP) vs app drive-away $59,899, gap $2,071. The gap is ~$2,071 on the RDP lines (Pure, GT; Mazda's RDP includes dealer delivery) and ~$508 on every special-offer line, replicating across grades, which confirms the list structure. July 2026 prices still current: no later Australian price change found; the Oct 2026 CarExpert 2027 update item is Europe-only.

batteryKwh.note: Usable capacity is unpublished. 17.8 kWh is gross (ADAC 'Batteriekapazität (Brutto)', heise 'Battery in kWh gross', auto motor und sport 'Energiegehalt brutto'). Estimate: heise could not discharge below 19% SoC (engine refires at 26%), so usable <= ~14.4 kWh; CarExpert real-world 55-60 km EV range at 22.1-25.2 kWh/100km trip-computer consumption implies 12.2-15.1 kWh delivered. CX-80 sibling holds the gross 17.8 on the same pack and should be aligned.

rangeKm.note: European WLTP electric range for the current (ab 11/25) car on 235/50R20, 63 km. The 12/24-11/25 cars showed 64 km on both 235/60R18 (https://www.adac.de/rund-ums-fahrzeug/autokatalog/marken-modelle/mazda/cx-60/kh/337820/) and 20-inch, so no wheel split is applied; this grade ships on 18-inch wheels. Australian 76 km is NEDC (CarExpert spec tables say 'Electric driving range (NEDC) 76km'), rejected by the direction test.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 14.0 / 63 x 100. Agrees with CarExpert's 2026 GT test (22.1 kWh/100km). The 14.8 kWh/100km Australian claim is the ADR utility-weighted label, not used.

combinedRangeKm.note: WLTP electric 63 km + 50 L tank / 7.7 L/100km x 100 (649 km). Tank 50 L from CarExpert's 2026 GT review and ADAC.

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: European WLTP 'Verbrauch kombiniert (WLTP) PHEV (Batterie leer)' charge-sustaining figure, identical on 18- and 20-inch cars. Previously held 8.5 was a review-based estimate. heise measured 7.2-8.5 L/100km without charging.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO green car = combined CO2 120 g/km or less; CX-60 P50e label is 49 g/km (CarExpert 2026 price-and-specs table).

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Mazda AU page: '477L of cargo space'. CarExpert 2024 P50e GT review confirms 477 L 'to rear package tray' for the PHEV. CarExpert's 2026 tables quote 570 L, the European roof-height VDA figure (ADAC 'Kofferraumvolumen normal 570 l'); the app's convention keeps the Australian 477.

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: CarExpert 2026 P50e GT review dimensions table '1726L (rear seats folded)'; same in ADAC for the PHEV.

towKg.note: CarExpert 2026 GT review 'Braked tow capacity 2500kg'; Mazda AU PHEV guide says braked towing 'remains 2500kg'.

warrantyYears.note: Five-year unlimited-km vehicle warranty; HV battery 8 years/160,000 km.

insuranceAnnual.note: Lowered with the $7,150 price cut. Anchored to mitsubishi-outlander-phev (ES $58,990 -> $1,650, Aspire $66,790 -> $1,750, Exceed $71,640 -> $1,800), mazda-cx-80-phev-touring ($68,100 -> $1,850) and kia-sorento-phev-s-awd ($70,880 -> $1,800), with a small premium-brand loading.

depreciationCurve.note: Kept the held curve, below the mainstream default. Evidence: the $7,150 list price cut in July 2026 erodes the resale value of earlier cars, and CarExpert reports drive-away deals well under list. Mazda PHEV convention: mazda-cx-80-phev holds a similar steep curve [1, 0.71, ...].

The gap is ~$2,071 on the RDP lines (Pure, GT; Mazda's RDP includes dealer delivery) and ~$508 on every special-offer line, replicating across grades, which confirms the list structure. July 2026 prices still current: no later Australian price change found; the Oct 2026 CarExpert 2027 update item is Europe-only.

batteryKwh.note: Usable capacity is unpublished. 17.8 kWh is gross (ADAC 'Batteriekapazität (Brutto)', heise 'Battery in kWh gross', auto motor und sport 'Energiegehalt brutto'). Estimate: heise could not discharge below 19% SoC (engine refires at 26%), so usable <= ~14.4 kWh; CarExpert real-world 55-60 km EV range at 22.1-25.2 kWh/100km trip-computer consumption implies 12.2-15.1 kWh delivered. CX-80 sibling holds the gross 17.8 on the same pack and should be aligned.

rangeKm.note: European WLTP electric range for the current (ab 11/25) car on 235/50R20, 63 km. The 12/24-11/25 cars showed 64 km on both 235/60R18 (https://www.adac.de/rund-ums-fahrzeug/autokatalog/marken-modelle/mazda/cx-60/kh/337820/) and 20-inch, so no wheel split is applied; this grade ships on 20-inch wheels. Australian 76 km is NEDC (CarExpert spec tables say 'Electric driving range (NEDC) 76km'), rejected by the direction test.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 14.0 / 63 x 100. Agrees with CarExpert's 2026 GT test (22.1 kWh/100km). The 14.8 kWh/100km Australian claim is the ADR utility-weighted label, not used.

combinedRangeKm.note: WLTP electric 63 km + 50 L tank / 7.7 L/100km x 100 (649 km). Tank 50 L from CarExpert's 2026 GT review and ADAC.

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: European WLTP 'Verbrauch kombiniert (WLTP) PHEV (Batterie leer)' charge-sustaining figure, identical on 18- and 20-inch cars. Previously held 8.5 was a review-based estimate. heise measured 7.2-8.5 L/100km without charging.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO green car = combined CO2 120 g/km or less; CX-60 P50e label is 49 g/km (CarExpert 2026 price-and-specs table).

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Mazda AU page: '477L of cargo space'. CarExpert 2024 P50e GT review confirms 477 L 'to rear package tray' for the PHEV. CarExpert's 2026 tables quote 570 L, the European roof-height VDA figure (ADAC 'Kofferraumvolumen normal 570 l'); the app's convention keeps the Australian 477.

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: CarExpert 2026 P50e GT review dimensions table '1726L (rear seats folded)'; same in ADAC for the PHEV.

towKg.note: CarExpert 2026 GT review 'Braked tow capacity 2500kg'; Mazda AU PHEV guide says braked towing 'remains 2500kg'.

warrantyYears.note: Five-year unlimited-km vehicle warranty; HV battery 8 years/160,000 km.

insuranceAnnual.note: Lowered with the $7,150 price cut. Anchored to mitsubishi-outlander-phev (ES $58,990 -> $1,650, Aspire $66,790 -> $1,750, Exceed $71,640 -> $1,800), mazda-cx-80-phev-touring ($68,100 -> $1,850) and kia-sorento-phev-s-awd ($70,880 -> $1,800), with a small premium-brand loading.

depreciationCurve.note: Kept the held curve, below the mainstream default. Evidence: the $7,150 list price cut in July 2026 erodes the resale value of earlier cars, and CarExpert reports drive-away deals well under list. Mazda PHEV convention: mazda-cx-80-phev holds a similar steep curve [1, 0.71, ...].

lowConfidence: mazda-cx-60-phev-*.batteryKwh: usable 14.0 kWh judged; only gross 17.8 is published anywhere found
mazda-cx-60-phev-*.consumptionKwhPer100km: derived from the judged usable battery (agrees with CarExpert's tested 22.1)
mazda-cx-60-phev-azami-sp / azami-takumi: these are $2,000 option packages on the Azami that Mazda prices as separate lines; kept as rows, could arguably be dropped
mazda-cx-60-phev-azami-sp.listPrice / azami-takumi.listPrice: $76,840 from GoAuto and CarExpert's July table plus Azami + $2,000 package; CarExpert's Aug table omits them
mazda-cx-60-phev-pure/evolve/touring.rangeKm: the current-WLTP 63 km is from a 20-inch car; the 18-inch car was 64 km under the previous certification
